statement: a file any number of levels deep under /etc must not be admitted either (the glob crosses /) (sem: SEM-gx-gate-328)
why: Cedar's `like` `*` matches any string and, unlike a shell glob, does not stop at `/` (primary: syntax-operators). ∴ `/etc/*` covers everything underneath, not just one level -- this pins the shipped pack's effective reach to that reading with an input rather than with prose. If the reading were reversed (one level only), this vector would tip onto the admit side. (sem: SEM-gx-gate-329)
spec_anchor: 34 AC-025 (/etc/**'s verbatim) / req/62 §2 (like's primary reference) (sem: SEM-gx-gate-330)

control.note: the same tail placed under a different root. Goes red if the pack starts refusing on 'contains the string /etc' -- the control that the refusal is an anchored (prefix) match (sem: SEM-gx-gate-331)
